name: Trainual
summary: Documents SOPs and runs new-hire onboarding, with AI that drafts and updates training docs from your own account context.
best_for: growing teams (roughly 10+ staff) that need to document SOPs and onboard new hires consistently instead of training by osmosis
skip_if: you're a team of two or three: a well-organized Notion or Google Doc captures your processes without the seat-band pricing
honest_knock: You cannot find out what it costs without booking a demo. All four plans (Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise) are quote-gated, and the single number the pricing page publishes is the one-time implementation fee of $1,000. The same page answers the sizing question plainly, best suited for companies with 25 to 1000 employees, so a small team is being told twice that it is not the buyer here: once by the fit range and once by a setup fee that arrives before the subscription does. Under a handful of staff, a shared doc may do. The product has also outgrown what the plan grid describes. In 2026 Trainual added an Operations suite (19 May) and a Performance suite (29 September), and the pricing page now sells three suites behind demo buttons. Whether a team that only wants SOPs and onboarding pays for the other two is exactly what a published price would answer, and none is published.

pricing.notes:
(re-read 2026-09-18 and again on 2026-10-05 on trainual.com/pricing) No prices at all. The page lists four plans — Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise, grouped under a Training, an Operations and a Performance suite — and every one of them carries a “Get a demo” button where a rate would be. The only figure the page publishes is a one-time implementation fee of $1,000, stated in its own FAQ alongside a 4–6 week engagement with an implementation specialist. The FAQ also answers the sizing question directly: “Trainual is best suited for companies with 25 - 1000 employees”, and says pricing varies with team size and the features you need. Pricing is quote-only. An earlier version of this entry carried monthly figures attributed to unnamed third-party sources; those are not on the vendor's page and could not be traced to a named source, so they have been removed rather than repeated.

There is also no self-serve way to try it. The FAQ question “Can I try Trainual before committing to a subscription?” is answered with an invitation to book a demo, not with a trial, so a sales conversation is the only route in. Two things are quantified beyond the fee: the implementation team aims to have interviews completed and content in the account within 10 business days, and 500+ templates are included, with 400+ expert-built courses sold separately as a premium courses add-on whose price the page does not give. Read on 5 October 2026, the Premium card lists an MCP server for custom AI agents, and Enterprise adds API access with custom integration support, access to SOC 2 security documentation and extended implementation and migration.

Read a third time on 21 October 2026 (served HTML): still no rate on any plan, the same $1,000 implementation fee and the same 25 - 1000 employee fit. The page is now organised around three suites, Training, Operations and Performance, each with its own Get a demo button, above a plan grid that still names Core, Pro, Premium and Enterprise. The per-plan video-storage and version-history figures we quoted from the 5 October reading did not appear in the served page this time, so they rest on that earlier reading. The FAQ now also answers the cancellation question: a cancelled plan runs to the end of the billing cycle with full access, and an account can instead be put on hold for up to three months.

open_questions.question: Are Trainual's Training, Operations and Performance suites priced separately?
Does the $1,000 implementation fee apply on every plan, and only once?
Can you publish a price, or a starting price, for the plans that are quote-only?
Can a customer cancel at any time, and what happens to an annual plan that is cancelled mid-term?
Which data can a customer export, in which formats, on which plans?
Where is customer data stored, and can a customer choose the region?
Is there a minimum number of seats or users on any plan?
